keys.AccountsV2.title: Coding accounts
keys.AccountsV2.modes_lead: Three ways an agent can run in this workspace. A workspace can allow more than one, and every screen shows which one did the work.
keys.AccountsV2.mode_workspace_sub: One API key in settings, shared by everyone
keys.AccountsV2.mode_personal_sub: Their own Claude Code. AlianHub never holds a key
keys.AccountsV2.mode_local_sub: Ollama or vLLM on your GPU, no external account
keys.AccountsV2.row_pays_workspace: The company. One bill, predictable, capped per agent.
keys.AccountsV2.row_pays_personal: The developer's own subscription. Workspace spend for this work is $0.
keys.AccountsV2.row_pays_local: Nobody, per run. Electricity and one GPU.
keys.AccountsV2.row_where_workspace: Server-side, from AlianHub. Needed for scheduled agents that run with nobody logged in.
keys.AccountsV2.row_where_personal: On the developer's machine. AlianHub only receives the result of the work: comments, status, PR link, hours.
keys.AccountsV2.row_can_workspace: Everything in the allow-list, including unattended and scheduled runs.
keys.AccountsV2.row_can_personal: Only what that person can do, only while they are at the keyboard. No scheduled runs.
keys.AccountsV2.row_can_local: Everything in the allow-list, but slower and weaker on hard reasoning.
keys.AccountsV2.row_offboarding_workspace: Nothing to do. The key is the company's.
keys.AccountsV2.row_offboarding_personal: Revoke their AlianHub token and the link dies. Their subscription and history stay theirs.
keys.AccountsV2.row_best_workspace: Scheduled agents: daily PM, reporter, smart assign.
keys.AccountsV2.row_best_personal: Hands-on coding work: your developers, on their own terms.
keys.AccountsV2.row_best_local: Regulated teams, air-gapped installs, or anyone who will not send work data out.
keys.AccountsV2.policy_read_only: READ ONLY, AN OWNER OR ADMIN SETS THIS
keys.AccountsV2.policy_workspace_effect: Server-side runs on the workspace key, including scheduled agents.
keys.AccountsV2.policy_personal_effect: Members may link their own CLI account and mint a scoped token.
keys.AccountsV2.policy_local_effect: Runs against a model inside your own network.
keys.AccountsV2.policy_need_one: At least one mode has to stay allowed.
keys.AccountsV2.policy_refusal_note: A mode that is off is refused with the reason shown, not hidden: linking an account and minting a token both check this policy before anything is written.
keys.AccountsV2.recommended_body: workspace key for the scheduled agents, because they are cheap and predictable; personal accounts for hands-on CLI coding work; and the self-hosted option available so a customer who refuses external models still gets the whole product. All three can run at once.
keys.AccountsV2.link_lead: Use your own Claude Code, Antigravity, Cursor or Codex account for work in AlianHub, then paste one command into your CLI.
keys.AccountsV2.link_form_lead: Pick how your agent work should run. This records the mode and provider against your user; it never asks for, stores or proxies a key.
keys.AccountsV2.sees_1: That a run happened, and which task it was on
keys.AccountsV2.sees_2: Elapsed time, and the hours written to your timesheet
keys.AccountsV2.sees_3: Every action taken through the allow-list, as an audit row
keys.AccountsV2.sees_4: The comments, subtasks, status moves and PR links your agent created
keys.AccountsV2.sees_5: Which account type produced each of them
keys.AccountsV2.stays_1: Your API key or subscription. AlianHub never receives one.
keys.AccountsV2.stays_2: Your prompts and chat history. Only the result reaches the server.
keys.AccountsV2.stays_3: Anything outside the projects your token is scoped to.
keys.AccountsV2.stays_4: Your provider spend and invoice. Nothing here reads them.
keys.AccountsV2.boundary_source: These are not promises added to a page. The left column is what the audit, run and timesheet rows actually store; the right column is what the code has no field for.
keys.AccountsV2.always_1: Every timer an agent starts is logged against you and stamped as agent time, not your own hours.
keys.AccountsV2.always_1_where: Modules/Agents/actions.js — timelog.start writes actorType, viaAccount and runId
keys.AccountsV2.always_2: Every allowed call and every refusal is written to the audit log with the account type and the token behind it.
keys.AccountsV2.always_3: A token scoped to projects can only see tasks in those projects.
keys.AccountsV2.always_3_where: Modules/Mcp/tools.js — scopeFilter restricts every tool to the token's projectIds
keys.AccountsV2.unlink_body: stops all agent work through your account and deactivates every agent token you hold here. Past comments, PRs and hours stay on their tasks; nothing is deleted.
keys.AccountsV2.field_email_hint: The address on your own provider account
keys.AccountsV2.no_modes_allowed: No mode is currently permitted for linking. Ask an owner or admin to change the policy.
keys.AccountsV2.summary_note: Counted from your own timesheet rows, runs and task links inside AlianHub. Your own spend sits on your provider account and nothing here reads it.
keys.AccountsV2.cli_comment_add: add AlianHub as an MCP server (any CLI agent)
keys.AccountsV2.cli_url_minted: This is the exact URL and token the server just returned. The token is not shown again.
keys.AccountsV2.cli_url_guess: The token appears here once you mint one, and the server returns the exact URL with it.
keys.AccountsV2.token_once: Copy this now. It is not shown again — only its hash is stored.
keys.AccountsV2.scope_all: Every project you can already open
keys.AccountsV2.scope_hint: A token scoped to one project cannot reach tasks outside it, whatever the CLI asks for.
keys.AccountsV2.token_name_required: Give the token a name so you can recognise it later.
keys.AccountsV2.no_tokens: No tokens yet. Mint one to connect a CLI agent.
keys.AccountsV2.token_inherits: A token inherits your permissions and then narrows them. It can never exceed what you can do, and delete, billing and member management are not in the registry at all.
keys.AccountsV2.self_hosted_note: Self-hosted means the MCP endpoint is on your network. Your code and your task data never leave it — only the model call does, and that can point at your own GPU.
keys.AccountsV2.attrib_lead: Person, tool, then account type — in that order, everywhere.
keys.AccountsV2.attrib_title: How it reads on the task
keys.AccountsV2.attrib_empty: No agent has run here yet. Start one from the agents list and it will appear with its account type.
keys.AccountsV2.by_source_source: Elapsed time on agent runs recorded in this workspace, split by the account each run went through. Human hours are counted separately on the timesheet.
keys.AccountsV2.why_split_body: velocity that quietly includes agent hours is a lie you will plan next quarter on. Keep the split visible and your estimates stay usable.
keys.AccountsV2.billing_q_body: when a client asks what the agent hours were, you can show the tasks, the links and who supervised them, and whether the run was billed to the workspace at all.
keys.AccountsV2.rules_lead: The awkward cases, decided in code rather than left to a conversation. Each rule names where it is enforced.
keys.AccountsV2.rule_leaves_body: Unlinking clears their account and deactivates every agent token they hold in this workspace. Their comments, PRs and logged hours stay on the tasks, attributed to them. Nothing is deleted.
keys.AccountsV2.rule_leaves_where: Modules/Agents/accounts.js — unlink sets active false on their agent tokens and unsets agentAccount
keys.AccountsV2.rule_lapses_body: A personal-mode CLI fails on their machine, and AlianHub never sees it: a CLI session creates no run record, so the task simply stays assigned to them with no new activity. Workspace-mode runs do record a failed status with the reason.
keys.AccountsV2.rule_lapses_where: Modules/Agents/runs.js — a failed status is written by the server-side run engine only
keys.AccountsV2.rule_contractor: A contractor wants their own account.
keys.AccountsV2.rule_contractor_body: Allowed, but their token can be scoped to the projects they are in. Then even the next-task and search tools only return tasks from those projects.
keys.AccountsV2.rule_contractor_where: Modules/Mcp/tools.js — scopeFilter adds the token's projectIds to every tool query
keys.AccountsV2.rule_two_people_body: Both can run agents on it. Each comment is stamped with the actor type, the agent and the account it came through, so a duplicate PR is obvious rather than mysterious.
keys.AccountsV2.rule_two_people_where: Modules/Agents/actions.js — task.comment stamps actorType, agentId and viaAccount on the comment
keys.AccountsV2.rule_require_mode: An admin can require a mode.
keys.AccountsV2.rule_require_mode_body: A regulated customer allows local only, and linking or minting anything else is refused with the reason shown rather than the option quietly disappearing.
keys.AccountsV2.rule_require_mode_where: Modules/Agents/accounts.js link and Modules/ApiTokens/controller.js createMcpToken both check the policy first
keys.AccountsV2.rule_unattended_body: A scheduled run through a personal account is refused, because nobody should be billed for a run they did not trigger while their laptop was shut.
keys.AccountsV2.rule_unattended_where: Modules/Agents/runs.js — canStart refuses a scheduled trigger when the account is personal
keys.AccountsV2.rule_allow_list_body: A personal account gets exactly the tools listed on the setup panel. The registry decision takes no account mode as an argument, so paying for your own model does not buy extra permissions.
keys.AccountsV2.rule_allow_list_where: Modules/Agents/registry.js — evaluate takes an action key and its params, never a mode
keys.AccountsV2.rule_reimbursement: Reimbursement is a report, not a feature.
keys.AccountsV2.rule_reimbursement_body: AlianHub counts tasks and hours through each person's account from its own rows. It never reads a provider invoice, and has no field to store one.
keys.AccountsV2.rule_reimbursement_where: Modules/Agents/accounts.js — monthlySummary reads timesheet, run and task-link rows only
keys.AccountsV2.rule_personal_spend: Personal spend is never the workspace's.
keys.AccountsV2.rule_personal_spend_body: A run through a personal account records the workspace cost as $0, keeps the estimate separately, and returns before touching the agent's monthly total.
keys.AccountsV2.rule_personal_spend_where: Modules/Agents/runs.js — recordSpend marks the run as not billed to the workspace
keys.AccountsV2.rule_local_spend: Local runs cost the workspace nothing.
keys.AccountsV2.rule_local_spend_body: Self-hosted runs are treated the same way as personal ones for billing: no workspace dollars, and no contribution to a cap.
keys.AccountsV2.rule_local_spend_where: Modules/Agents/runs.js — recordSpend excludes both personal and local from billing
keys.AccountsV2.rule_revoke: Revoking stops future runs and keeps the history.
keys.AccountsV2.rule_revoke_body: Revoke here deactivates the token, so it stops authenticating immediately. Every audit row, comment and time log it already wrote stays exactly where it is.
keys.AccountsV2.rule_revoke_where: Modules/ApiTokens/controller.js — verifyToken only accepts an active token; audit rows live in their own collection
keys.AccountsV2.rule_caps: A cap pauses the agent, it does not fail quietly.
keys.AccountsV2.rule_caps_body: When workspace-billed spend reaches an agent's monthly cap the agent is paused with the reason recorded, and the next run is refused with that same reason.
keys.AccountsV2.rule_caps_where: Modules/Agents/runs.js — recordSpend pauses at the cap and canStart refuses once it is reached
keys.AccountsV2.never_title: Absent from the registry, in every mode
keys.AccountsV2.never_body: These are not permissions that have been switched off. They are not in the action list at all, so a compromised token has nothing to switch on, and an attempt is refused with an audit id.
keys.AccountsV2.undecided_1_body: The numbers above are computed on request and there is no export endpoint, so a reimbursement claim is currently a manual read rather than a file.
keys.AccountsV2.undecided_2: Per-person visibility of the full call list.
keys.AccountsV2.undecided_2_body: Every call is audited, but who may read those rows is governed by the existing audit permissions. There is no per-member setting to share or hide the detail.
keys.AccountsV2.why_shape_body: The alternative — the company buys keys for everyone and proxies every call — puts AlianHub in the middle of every prompt a developer writes. That is a privacy problem, a cost problem and a support problem, and developers work around it by using their own CLI outside the tool anyway. Let them keep their own account and their own habits; AlianHub's job is to hand over a good brief and to record what came back.
keys.PipelineV2.title: The pipeline
keys.PipelineV2.lead: One task, five stages, one hard stop. What an agent may do, what it may only propose and what it cannot reach are read from the action registry — not written down here.
keys.PipelineV2.empty_title: No agent has worked a task yet
keys.PipelineV2.empty_body: The pipeline draws itself from real runs and proposals. Start a run from an agent and this fills in.
keys.PipelineV2.audit_restricted: Audit rows are visible to Owners and Admins.
keys.PipelineV2.s1_body: A person writes the brief and assigns it.
keys.PipelineV2.s1_none: This task has no brief yet.
keys.PipelineV2.s2_body: The agent reads the brief, works, and keeps the task and the timer current. It may set In progress or In review — never Done.
keys.PipelineV2.s2_none: No run on this task yet.
keys.PipelineV2.s3_body: The agent attaches the PR and posts what it found. CI keeps running wherever it runs today — AlianHub reads the result, it never builds.
keys.PipelineV2.s3_none: Nothing linked to this task, and no CI source is connected.
keys.PipelineV2.s4_body: {actions} is propose-only: an agent may ask, {gate} decides in the AI Inbox.
keys.PipelineV2.s4_body_none: The registry has no gated action right now, so nothing can be proposed for staging.
keys.PipelineV2.s4_none: No staging deploy has been proposed for this task.
keys.PipelineV2.s4_none_registry: No gated action exists in the registry.
keys.PipelineV2.s5_body: {keys} are absent from the registry. Not disabled — absent, so there is no flag to switch on.
keys.PipelineV2.s5_body_reachable: A deploy or merge action is present in the registry. Review it: production is meant to be unreachable for agents.
keys.PipelineV2.s5_none: {n} actions are named as never reachable.
keys.PipelineV2.note_a_title: What AlianHub contributes at each stage.
keys.PipelineV2.note_a_body: Stage 1 gives the agent a brief instead of a ticket. Stages 2 and 3 keep the task, timesheet and burndown current without anyone typing an update. Stage 4 turns "who approved that deploy?" into a row in the audit log. Stage 5 is outside the agent's reach, so the answer to "can it ship to prod?" is no, structurally.
keys.PipelineV2.note_b_body: Nothing changes in your pipeline. AlianHub would read status from the PR and the deploy webhook — it never runs your builds.
keys.PipelineV2.staging_never: No staging deploy has been approved
keys.PipelineV2.notes_none: No agent has drafted release notes. A drafting skill would file one here as a proposal you approve — until then, this is what has been marked Done.
keys.PipelineV2.no_done_tasks: Nothing has been marked Done since the last release.
keys.PipelineV2.staging_rule: {keys} is propose-only in the registry: an agent may ask, {gate} approves it, and the decision lands in the audit log.
keys.PipelineV2.staging_rule_none: The registry has no gated action, so no agent can propose a staging deploy.
keys.PipelineV2.staging_none: No staging deploy has been proposed.
keys.PipelineV2.check_human: Every Done was set by a person — agents cannot set Done
keys.PipelineV2.check_ci: CI result unknown — no CI source is connected
keys.PipelineV2.no_target_body: AlianHub has no deploy integration, so there is no production button to press here. Deploying stays in whatever tool you deploy with today; this screen records who decided what.
keys.PipelineV2.rel_foot: Agents can get you a branch, findings and a clean staging run. The last step stays a decision with a name on it — and the name lands in the audit log next to the version.
keys.PipelineV2.hist_none: Nothing has been proposed or refused yet.
keys.PipelineV2.hist_none_restricted: Nothing proposed yet. Refused attempts are visible to Owners and Admins.
keys.PipelineV2.side_note: This screen reads what AlianHub already records. It does not run builds, and it cannot deploy.
keys.ProvenanceV2.badge_agent_hint: An agent did the work and a person checked it.
keys.ProvenanceV2.badge_mixed_hint: A person and an agent both worked on it.
keys.ProvenanceV2.badge_unchecked_hint: An agent did the work and nobody has checked it.
keys.ProvenanceV2.filter_hint: Agent-built and unchecked is the one worth pinning to a dashboard.
keys.ProvenanceV2.first_pass_note: First-pass = closed without going back to In progress. Agent work needs a second pass more often; that is useful to know, not a reason to stop.
keys.ProvenanceV2.velocity_line: Velocity reads two ways: {total} points closed in all, {human} by people alone. Plan the next sprint on the human line if your agent access might change.
keys.ProvenanceV2.margin_line: Cost per closed task: {cost} overall, {human} where only people worked, {agent} where an agent did.
keys.ProvenanceV2.margin_no_rate: Set a blended cost rate on the project contract to see cost per closed task.
keys.ProvenanceV2.unchecked_line: {n} closed with agent work nobody checked.
keys.ProvenanceV2.why: Every field here is filled by an action someone already took — the work log, the review, the close. In a year, teams that can say which work an agent did, and who checked it, will be able to answer a client, an auditor and their own retro.
keys.ProvenanceV2.empty_sub: The split appears as tasks are finished.
keys.ProvenanceV2.ext_sources_sub: what an agent may read from each
keys.ProvenanceV2.ext_no_mirror: AlianHub does not mirror external tables. A linked row stays in its source — comment on it, link tasks to it and filter on it here; edits happen where the data lives.
keys.ProvenanceV2.ext_hand_off: Hand a task to a coding agent
keys.ProvenanceV2.ext_no_account_sub: Link one to hand tasks to Claude Code, Cursor or your own CLI.
keys.ProvenanceV2.ext_handed_note: Status moves to In progress and findings land as a comment. Merging is still a human's job.
keys.ProvenanceV2.ext_same_treatment: External agents get the same treatment as yours: allow-listed actions, everything through the AI Inbox, full audit.

Nothing recorded on a time log says which client it was entered from, and a split drawn from a guess would be worse than none.
